title: sin(1)'s partial sums converge to the constructed value sinOne
statement: CReal.Converges CReal.sinSeriesPartial CReal.sinOne -- mirrors CReal.cosOneConverges exactly, including building GENERICALLY over a bound (k, h) rather than the concrete k_final that CReal.sinOne's own construction uses internally, for the same stack-overflow-avoidance reason declare_cos_one_converges documents (a concrete Nat witness fed into an exists_intro's argument check can drive an unbounded partial evaluation against a still-symbolic index; staying generic over a bound variable keeps the arithmetic stuck against two free variables and never runs).

evidence.supports: CReal.sinOneConverges is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_dependency_inventory -- sinOneConverges 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^CReal\.sinOneConverges[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: build_creal_prelude admits CReal.sinOneConverges through the trusted Kernel::add_declaration gate. theorem_dependency_inventory exits non-zero for a named filter matching nothing; grep -c asserts the exact tab-anchored line. --release is MANDATORY: this tool also builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the creal prelude's trusted surface is empty, which bounds CReal.sinOneConverges
evidence.notes: Re-measured on this tree: creal: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0, exits 0 printing 'ok: creal trusted surface = 0'. That bounds every declaration in the creal environment, including CReal.sinOneConverges, since a declaration cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. --require-axiom-free <name> errors for a prelude never built by this run rather than silently passing on zero rows. --release is MANDATORY here.

provenance.source: canonical type read via kernel_declaration_projection's own UNFILTERED emit mode (cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection, no --require-declaration flag), which prints, per constructed prelude, one TSV row per declaration whose last field is kernel.render_lean(declaration.ty()) -- the same Kernel::render_lean canonical form nat_theorem_inventory prints, just not filtered to Declaration::Theorem. That output was piped to a scratchpad file and the exact row for this declaration's own prelude label was extracted and injected here programmatically (a Python script reading the TSV, never hand-transcribed); direct theorem dependencies were cross-read from the same run's direct_theorems column (field 6) and matched against the ledger's own registered kernel_theorem/formal.statement names to populate depends_on. No new probe binary was written for this batch; crates/ source was not touched to produce this batch.

notes: Building block for CReal.sinOne_alternating_lower and CReal.sinOne_alternating_upper (this batch), which instantiate CReal.alternatingLowerBound/alternatingUpperBound (this batch) with this convergence fact as the limit hypothesis. depends_on lists every registered building block; CReal.geomCauchyOrderedHalf, CReal.mul_sumRange, CReal.regular_of_scaled_cauchy, CReal.speedup_close and CReal.sumRange_cauchy_dominated_ordered_normalized are unregistered private/carrier lemmas.
